blocks.title: Después de este pdf sabrás
bullets: contar lo que alguien dijo, con say y tell
poner los tiempos un paso atrás
hacer preguntas indirectas con if y con palabras interrogativas, sin do
contar peticiones y órdenes con asked / told someone to

head: Regla
Ejemplo
rows: sin persona, o con to + persona
She said (that) she was tired. She said to me that ...
siempre con una persona justo detrás
She told me (that) she was tired.
tell the truth, tell a lie, tell a story, tell the time

blocks.title: Me dijo = He told me
blocks.text: El español usa decir para las dos cosas. Recuerda: si justo después viene una persona, se usa tell: Me dijo que ... = He told me that ..., nunca He said me. Y decir la verdad, decir una mentira, contar un cuento = tell the truth, tell a lie, tell a story.
Después de un verbo en pasado (said, told, asked) el tiempo suele ir un paso atrás, como en español (dijo que estaba cansada). También cambian los pronombres y las expresiones de tiempo.

head: Lo que dijo
Indirecto
Tiempo
rows: She said she had seen the film.
She said she would call me.

blocks.title: ¿Cuándo no se cambia?
blocks.text: Si sigue siendo verdad, el tiempo puede quedarse igual: She said she lives in Leiden (todavía vive allí). Y después de un verbo en presente no cambia nada: He says he's busy.
En una pregunta indirecta va el orden normal (sujeto – verbo), sin do, does ni did y sin signo de interrogación. Las preguntas de sí o no llevan if o whether.

head: Pregunta directa
Indirecta
Español
rows: He asked me where I lived.
She asked if I was hungry.
Can you tell me what time it is?
They asked whether I had seen him.
Me preguntaron si lo había visto.

blocks.title: Orden normal: where the toilets are
blocks.text: El español mantiene el orden de la pregunta (¿Sabes dónde están los servicios?). El inglés no: Do you know where the toilets are?, nunca where are the toilets. Y el si de una pregunta indirecta es if o whether: No sé si viene = I don't know if he's coming.

head: Directo
Indirecto
Español
rows: She asked me to help her.
He told us to sit down.
My boss told me not to be late.
Mi jefe me dijo que no llegara tarde.
He said me that he was ill.
He told me that he was ill.
Con una persona justo detrás: tell.
She asked me where did I live.
She asked me where I lived.
Pregunta indirecta: sin did, orden normal.
Can you tell me where is the station?
Can you tell me where the station is?
Pregunta indirecta: el sujeto delante del verbo.
He told that he was tired.
He said that he was tired.
She asked me that if I wanted tea.
She asked me if I wanted tea.
El si de una pregunta indirecta: if, sin that delante (no: preguntó que si).
He told me don't touch it.
He told me not to touch it.

blocks.text: Completa con la palabra que falta. Las respuestas están en la última página.

items.full: She told me she was leaving.

items.q: He ______ that he didn't like fish.
items.full: He said that he didn't like fish.
"I'm busy." — She said she was busy.

items.q: "I'll help you." — He said he ______ help me.
items.full: "I'll help you." — He said he would help me.

items.q: "I saw it." — She said she ______ seen it.
items.full: "I saw it." — She said she had seen it.

items.q: He asked me ______ I was married.
items.full: He asked me if I was married.

items.q: Can you tell me where the toilets ______?
items.full: Can you tell me where the toilets are?

items.q: She asked me ______ close the window.
items.full: She asked me to close the window.

items.q: The doctor told me ______ to eat too much sugar.
items.full: The doctor told me not to eat too much sugar.

items.q: "I can drive." — He said he ______ drive.
items.full: "I can drive." — He said he could drive.

items.q: I don't know ______ she will come.
items.full: I don't know if she will come.

items.a: She asked me where I lived.
I don't know if he's coming.

items.q: Mi madre me pidió que la ayudara.
items.a: My mother asked me to help her.
